aiExplanation: This code counts how many days two people, Alice and Bob, are in the same place at the same time, given their arrival and departure dates as `"MM-DD"` strings. It first builds a `prefixSum` array where each entry holds the total number of days in all the months before it, so the `convert` helper can turn any date string into a single **day-of-year number** by adding the day to the prefix total for its month. The main function starts with a quick **early exit**: since the strings are zero-padded, they can be compared lexicographically, and if one person leaves before the other arrives there is no overlap, so it returns `0`. Otherwise it converts all four dates to day numbers and computes the overlap as `min(end1, end2) - max(start1, start2) + 1`, which is the standard formula for the length of the intersection of two **inclusive ranges**: the shared period begins on the later arrival and ends on the earlier departure, with the `+ 1` counting both endpoints.
